correctness.rationale: The proof reduces graph-distance transport exactly to forced leaf-edge flux plus optimal complete-core flux. Two explicit invariant heat blocks and sign inequalities yield exact pendant and core edge norms. The strict edge comparison and nonzero spanning-tree flux prove the unique positive-time extremizers. The derivative is a strictly decreasing exponential sign bracket with initial value n-3, proving the threshold and unique peak. The strict factor-two bound follows from alpha*A>2*C and A-C<2; evaluating at t=(log n)/n gives the sharp limit. The unpacked standard-library verifier passed 55 heat-kernel/time cases and 1,815 edge evaluations, plus 68 independent dual maximizations. Finite tests are supporting evidence, not the proof of universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The known corona Laplacian eigenvalues are credited, not claimed. The exact graph-Lipschitz operator norm requires a different transport optimization that determines the winning edge type and every extremizer. The n=4 amplification threshold and sharp unattained factor-two envelope do not follow solely from the published spectrum. Comparisons against directly inspected graph heat-gradient theory and nearby transport calculations did not identify a stronger result implying the full statement. Publication-priority risk remains for unindexed work.

value.rationale: The corona K_n circle K_1 is a standard natural family with a known spectrum, making exact Lipschitz behavior a motivated unresolved comparison. The theorem determines the whole non-Hilbert norm profile for every n and t, shows a strict switch in the determining edge type, identifies all extremizers, proves the first amplification case n=4 and gives a sharp, unattained factor-two family envelope. These are structural properties and not a routine eigenspectrum re-expression or an arbitrary isolated parameter value.
